A destination that refuses your credentials no longer reads as a destination that is merely empty, and the images left behind by a container update are explained at the switch that turns the update on.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A refused repository was reported as one that did not exist yet** ([#192](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/192)). A connection test against a `rest-server` started with `--private-repos` came back "reachable, not initialized" while the server was in fact answering 401 Unauthorized. That reads as "the destination is fine, it is just empty" and leaves nothing to act on. restic prefixes `unable to open config file` onto a transport failure exactly as it does onto a missing config, and BombVault was believing the prefix instead of the status code. Measured against a live rest-server before changing anything: a wrong password, and a URL whose first path segment is not the htpasswd user, both produce that same 401 wearing that same prefix. A 401 or 403 now reports as refused, so the two commonest setup mistakes stop hiding behind a reassuring word.

## 🎨 Design

- **The "update after successful backup" toggle says what it leaves behind** ([#193](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/193)). Reported as a Docker page full of orphan images after the first night with the option on for every container, which the internet reads as the mark of a failed update. It is the opposite. Docker keeps the image the container ran on before, now untagged, Unraid lists untagged images as orphans, and that old image is what makes a rollback cheap, since a snapshot restores a container's data and not the image it ran on. The toggle now says both that the leftover is normal and that **Settings → Paths & Storage → Image Cleanup & Update Status** carries a switch for deleting it. That switch existed all along and was too well hidden to be found from the place where the decision is actually made.

## 🌐 Translations

- The new interface string is translated into all 42 languages. Each one names the menu path in its own wording, read out of that language's own menu strings rather than translated a second time.
